Nuclear downloadThe zip file. Every page, every PDF, every ebook, and the important files.

13 November 2026. The permanent itemised list. Each title opens the original file in the GitHub archive.

The official records

This is the full list of the official government documents and related correspondence. There are 1333 files. The copies were too large to publish inside this site, so each title opens the same file in the GitHub archive. 278 have a date in the file name. 669 name an agency in the file name or the folder.

Each title is the date, the agency, and the reason, in that order. Those three things are read from the file name. Where the file name does not state them, the title says so. Nothing in this list was guessed from inside the document. The line under the title is the original file name.

Download this itemised list · Download the hash index

The genesis command, and what the opened letters say

This reading was made by applying one command to the highest letters, and only to the pages that were opened. The command is the genesis of the paragraphs below. It was not applied to the other files in the list of 1,333. A file name is not the document.

Read only what this document says. Do not add a motive the words do not support. Extract every stated purpose, every decision, every refusal, every delay, every condition, and every omission. Then say, in one paragraph, what detriment to me follows from those words if they are carried out. If the detriment is written as a purpose, quote it. If it is not written, but follows from the decision, call it the consequence, not a secret order. Name the office, the date, and the sentence. If the document does not show detriment, say so.

None of the decisions below writes a purpose to harm. Where there is a detriment, it is the consequence of the decision.

  1. Victorian Ombudsman, Ben Calder, 5 August 2021. He confirms a phone call about Mercy Health, the Mental Health Complaints Commissioner and a decision of the Office of the Victorian Information Commissioner. He writes that the Ombudsman can consider those complaints under the Ombudsman Act 1973 and “we are unable to provide you with legal advice or representation.” The pages read say he will make enquiries. They do not close the complaint. No detriment is decided in the sentences read.
  2. Victorian Ombudsman, 5 October 2021. It was “not justifiable to continue to deal with your complaint,” because further involvement was “unlikely to achieve a practical outcome” and there were “insufficient grounds” for more enquiries. The letter says consideration “has concluded” and “I have closed your case,” and that further correspondence “may not be responded to unless it raises new issues.” A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the complaint is closed.
  3. Victorian Ombudsman, 14 June 2022, FOI/22/14. The office apologises for the delay and says the notification link from the Department of Justice had failed. The documents sought are complaint and enquiry records. Section 29A of the Ombudsman Act means the FOI Act does not apply, and “I decline to release them.” A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that those records are not released.
  4. Commonwealth Ombudsman, Judi, reply to the email of 10 November 2021. “The information provided does not alter my assessment that your disclosure does not meet the threshold for a public interest disclosure under section 26 of the PID Act.” Then: “Our Office will not communicate with you further regarding the matters contained in your disclosure, outside of the review process” in the letter of 29 October 2021. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the office stops corresponding on that disclosure.
  5. File indexed as the IBAC rejection of 18 November 2021, PID-2021-400008. The pages read record that the authorised officer decided the disclosure “does not satisfy the requirements” of section 26, and treat the email as a request to review that decision. They also say that if the abusive comments continue, “we may have to limit your contact with us in future.” That limit is a condition, not the purpose of the disclosure decision. The review outcome is not in the sentences read.
  6. Commonwealth Ombudsman, 16 September 2022. “I am unable to progress this matter as an internal public interest disclosure.” The written reasons are that the office is not an authorised internal recipient under section 34, and that the PID Act does not apply to the alleged conduct of state agencies and private entities. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that those claims are not progressed under the PID scheme.
  7. Commonwealth Ombudsman, 22 March 2023, PID-2023-100007. “I am unable to progress this matter as an internal public interest disclosure.” The written reason is that the office is not an authorised internal recipient under section 34. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the office will not investigate the matters listed in the letter.
  8. Department of Social Services, 18 July 2023. “I will not be allocating the matter for investigation.” The written reason is section 26(1)(a): a public interest disclosure can only be made by a public official, and the department had no record of employment. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that DSS will not investigate.
  9. Department of Health and Aged Care, disclosure of 19 October 2023. “I have decided not to allocate this disclosure for handling by an agency,” under section 44(3). The written reasons are that it was not made to an authorised recipient and that the conduct does not relate to that department. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that Health will not handle it.
  10. National Disability Insurance Agency, 15 December 2021. A delegate agrees to the section 48 request to review the plan and says the agency will make contact within 14 days. This letter does not show a detriment. The decision is to review.
  11. National Disability Insurance Agency, 1 June 2023, Lead Delegate Kate P, participant 430938559. “You are not eligible for Specialist Disability Accommodation.” “Supported Independent Living (SIL): not suitable for SIL.” Drop-in daily-living support is approved. The written reason is that the information did not meet the SDA criteria, after Amy Cavenett’s report of 3 May 2023. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that SDA and SIL are refused.
  12. National Disability Insurance Agency, reply concerning the disclosure of 18 April 2023. The agency apologises that the allocation decision was not made within the 14 days the Act requires, because of the number of documents. A purpose to harm is not written. The detriment in this letter is the delay. The letter does not itself refuse the disclosure.
  13. Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, 23 March 2022, RQ22/00794. “I have decided to grant the Department an extension of time under s 15AB(2) of the FOI Act to 8 April 2022,” because the request was complex and voluminous. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet is given until 8 April 2022.
  14. Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, 22 April 2022, RQ22/01369. The department did not decide the request of 7 April 2022 in time, so “the FOI Act deems that the Department has refused your request.” The Commissioner then grants further time to 14 April 2022. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence of the deeming provision is that the request stands as refused unless that further time is applied.
  15. Australian Human Rights Commission, 4 July 2023. The Commission writes that it does not have power to “grant you whistleblower status,” and that being a whistleblower is not a protected attribute under the anti-discrimination laws it administers. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the Commission will not confer that status.
  16. Office of the Official Secretary to the Governor-General, reply to the letter of 8 September 2024. “The Governor-General is unable to advise on this matter.” A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that Government House will not advise or intervene.
  17. Attorney-General’s Department, A Riley, 19 September 2023, MC23-028244. No decision on the ASIO allegation. The Prime Minister referred the email of 5 July 2023. The department tells the writer to take the ASIO concern to the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security and the other concerns to the Commonwealth Ombudsman. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the department does not examine the conduct.
  18. NSW Trustee and Guardian, 16 October 2024, section 122(2), Matter 658238. The notice certifies that the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal committed management of the estate of Barran Resonance Dodger to the NSW Trustee and Guardian, and that the estate remains under management. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the estate is not in his control.
  19. NSW Trustee and Guardian, notice applying from 11 November 2025, Ford Territory S797CDP. “We recently decided to dispose of the Ford Territory.” The written purpose is “to help provide you with enough money to cover budgeted expenses.” The written reasons are that evidence of how the vehicle was obtained had not been provided, and that the trust account could not afford it. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the vehicle is taken and disposed of.
  20. Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, tracking code 43704714. This is a privacy complaint form, not a decision. It does not show a detriment imposed by the OAIC.
  21. Comcare file of 25 May 2021, claim 1326583. The pages read are an email to the claims managers before a decision expected the next day. They are not Comcare’s decision. No detriment is imposed by the office in the text read.
  22. File of 11 April 2021, indexed as a rejection of the CDDA scheme. The pages read are the writer’s own urgent email. They do not contain the department’s refusal. No office sentence of detriment was in the text read.
  23. Australian Small Business and Family Enterprise Ombudsman, 15 October 2021. The email says a letter from the Hon Bruce Billson is attached. The decision in that attachment was not in the text that could be read. No detriment sentence is quoted.

Across the decisions that were in the letters, the office declines, closes, delays, withholds the documents, refuses the accommodation, or takes the estate or the car, and it gives a statutory or administrative reason. Not one of these letters writes that the purpose of the decision is to cause detriment. The detriment is the consequence of what the letter does.

The next letters, under the same command

These are the documents that sit under the first set: the plan, the restriction, the compensation decision, the disclosure decision, the guardianship order, the injury notice, the ban, and the police release. The same command was applied. Two files that were looked for are not in this list. The NCAT order of 24 December 2024 was not at the archive address. A department letter refusing the CDDA scheme, as distinct from the email asking for it, was not in the pages read.

  1. National Disability Insurance Agency, plan starting 20 November 2025, participant 430938559. “This plan’s total funding amount is $366,406.69.” It runs to 19 November 2026. Plan-managed Core is $274,255.84. “The delivery of plan management must only be provided by WA South West Plan Managers.” “The delivery of specialist support coordination must only be provided by Diversitas WA.” In the section about him the plan records: “I am 52 years old and currently have no stable accommodation.” A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence of the limits is that the money and the coordination are confined to those providers. The absence of a stable address is recorded in the plan. The funding is on the paper.
  2. Commonwealth Ombudsman, Belinda, A/g Senior Assistant Ombudsman, 8 August 2025, complaint 2024-706941. “Decision to restrict your contact with the Commonwealth Ombudsman.” The written reason is that 229 emails were sent in 12 months, that most were outside jurisdiction or contained offensive images and abusive language, and that a request of 3 January 2025 to stop was not followed. “Your emails will be filtered and held on receipt and will not reach the intended mailbox.” “My decision to restrict your contact with this Office is effective immediately and will last for 6 months.” The expiry written in the letter is 8 February 2026. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that email to the office does not arrive for those six months.
  3. Comcare, 26 May 2021, the determination outcome on the workers’ compensation claim. “Comcare have declined liability on your workers’ compensation claim on the basis Comcare are not satisfied you are an ‘employee’ in accordance with the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988.” A reconsideration could be asked for within 30 days. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that liability is declined. The pages read are the email that attaches the determination. They are the decision as it was sent.
  4. National Disability Insurance Agency, public interest disclosure, emails of 18 April 2023. “I have decided not to allocate the handling of your disclosure to an agency under section 43(2) of the PID Act.” The written reason is that there was no reasonable basis to treat it as an internal disclosure, because the officer was not satisfied he was a public official. “I will not take any further action in relation to the emails.” A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that the disclosure is not investigated.
  5. NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal, Guardianship Division, S L Handebo, Principal Member, decision 9 October 2025, filed 18 March 2026. The guardianship order of 16 October 2024 is reviewed. “The Public Guardian is appointed as the guardian.” It is a continuing order for 3 years and a limited order. The functions are accommodation, “to decide where Barran Dodger may reside”; health care; medical and dental consent; services; and legal services, including authority to instruct lawyers. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is that those decisions are no longer his. This is the guardianship order. It is not the financial-management notice already set out above.
  6. Department of Social Services, 1 July 2022, IR8415987. The file is an automated email: “Opened - [IR8415987] - Report of 'fatal' injury in which provider & participant was revived.” It is not the medical report. It does not show a detriment. It shows that an item by that name was opened.
  7. Services Australia, 19 March 2025, reference 305 689 451X. “We have made a decision about how you can contact us.” The written reason is behaviour at the Tuggeranong Service Centre on 6 March 2025. “From 20 March 2025 to 31 July 2025” contact is limited to named officers by a stated telephone option. The letter says that during the restriction he cannot enter Services Australia premises, or the places where Centrelink, Medicare or Child Support are offered, or the associated carparks. “If you enter any Services Australia premises, places or associated carparks without an agreed appointment, the police may be called and you may be prosecuted for criminal trespass.” A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence is exclusion from the premises, and police and prosecution if the condition is broken.
  8. Victoria Police, freedom of information 70120/20, McLean. The pages are marked “Released under freedom of information.” What can be read is “Not Relevant,” and exemptions under section 33(1) and section 31(1)(a). The pages read do not contain a narrative of an assault or a decision against him. The omission is the redaction. A purpose to harm is not written. The consequence of the exemptions is that the record of what police held is not visible in this copy.

The same limit holds. These letters record the plan, the restriction, the declined claim, the unallocated disclosure, the guardian’s functions, the opened injury item, the ban, and the redacted police release. None of them writes that the purpose was to cause detriment. The detriment, where there is one, is the consequence of the decision.
